facts.claim: MDN's What is JavaScript article says JavaScript is a scripting language that enables you to create dynamically updating content.
React's State: A Component's Memory guide says that in React, the component-specific memory is called state.
React's Learn guide says a component is a piece of the UI (user interface) that has its own logic and appearance.
MDN's Web Storage API article says each origin has its own separate storage area, and that localStorage data persists even when the browser is closed and reopened.

MDN's Storage quotas and eviction criteria article says best-effort data persists as long as the origin is below its quota, the device has enough storage space, and the user does not delete the data through the browser's settings.
The TypeScript handbook says the goal of TypeScript is to be a static typechecker for JavaScript programs, meaning a tool that runs before your code runs.
GitHub's guide to committing in GitHub Desktop says that when you make a commit you must include a commit message that briefly describes the changes.
GitHub's guide to committing in GitHub Desktop says Git assigns each commit a unique ID, called a SHA or hash, that identifies the specific changes, when they were made and who created them.
MDN's Web Storage API article says all data stored in a private window is deleted when the browser or browser tab is closed.
MDN's Storage quotas and eviction criteria article says the Web Storage API provides mechanisms to store string-only key and value pairs.

MDN's Storage quotas and eviction criteria article says that when the browser needs to evict best-effort data it does so without interrupting the user, and the user can delete the data through the browser's settings.

MDN's Array.prototype.filter() page says the method calls a provided function once for each element and constructs a new array of all the values for which the function returns a value that coerces to true.
MDN's Array.prototype.reduce() page says the return value of the callback becomes the value of the accumulator parameter on the next invocation.
GitHub's guide to committing in GitHub Desktop says that when you make a commit you must include a commit message that briefly describes the changes.

GitHub's guide to resetting to a commit in GitHub Desktop says resetting to a commit restores the changes in the subsequent commits to your working directory and resets the branch to the selected commit.
GitHub's guide to resetting to a commit in GitHub Desktop says you can then make changes before committing again, or discard the changes that you do not want to keep.
MDN's How the web works article says that when a client wants to access a webpage, a copy of the webpage code is downloaded from the server to the client machine, where it is rendered by the browser.

Cloudflare's build configuration guide for Pages says you should provide a build command to tell Cloudflare Pages how to build your application, and that you may tell it where the output files will be located.
Cloudflare's Pages documentation says you can deploy a Pages project by connecting it to your Git provider.
Alibaba Cloud's help centre describes individual identity verification for an account.
